name: TypeSafe Jev for calls that only pick a label
gain: TypeSafe's words: end-to-end response time of 70ms-500ms, "40x-200x faster" than frontier models on these queries (vendor claim). There is no independent study on this page.
how: POST /v1/systemone with the state and a Choice, Score or Noul question. Gate on the returned confidence, and keep today's call as the fallback below the gate. Pin a version such as jev-1.14.0 once a threshold is tuned.
replaces: A chat call asked to classify, route, answer yes or no, or score.
trade_offs: Weak on maths, counting and date comparison: TypeSafe says to keep those in code.
English is where accuracy is best; test other languages on your own content first.
A new vendor and a new key. jev-latest moves when a release ships, so its answers can change without a code change.
The default limit is 64k tokens per request and 32k per question.
price: $0.042 per 1M input tokens; output tokens are free.
usage_signal: Usage and Cost API: high call count with few output tokens per call

gain_model.formula: calls * (current_cost_per_call - decision_cost_per_call), plus p50 latency difference

inputs.name: calls
inputs.source: the product's usage data or the bill

inputs.name: current_cost_per_call
inputs.source: the product's usage data or the bill

inputs.name: decision_cost_per_call
inputs.source: the product's usage data or the bill

test_recipe.what_to_compare: agreement with the current call, p50 latency, fallback rate

verify_rule: Cost line and p50 for that call over 14 days; fallback rate under the gate

change_recipe.how: POST /v1/systemone with the state and a Choice, Score or Noul question. Gate on the returned confidence, and keep today's call as the fallback below the gate. Pin a version such as jev-1.14.0 once a threshold is tuned.
change_recipe.left_off: Nothing else changes; the new path sits behind a setting until a person turns it on
